nodes.expected: Per-seed predictions differ from the parent, with strongest gains on context-heavy slices and positive paired portfolio contribution if temporal context repairs residual tab-specific misranking.
nodes.hypothesis: Adding legal temporal context fields that DeepFM can cross with user/item ids will improve within-user ranking and likely add marginal portfolio gain by correcting context-specific ordering errors without using any post-exposure inference feature.
nodes.label: temporal-context categorical augmentation
nodes.lesson: Legal temporal context can alter rankings but, here, its signal was too weak and inconsistent to justify keeping it as a standalone refinement.
nodes.result: The experiment successfully changed predictions, so the legal_temporal_context operator was active and consumed by the unchanged DeepFM pipeline. On standalone validation it produced only a very small mean gain over the search parent/incumbent (delta_primary about +0.00053), but the paired 95% CI crossed zero, so the improvement is not statistically reliable. Slice diagnostics show mixed effects rather than the expected broad context repair: gains appeared for some tabs and user-history/popularity segments, but several context-heavy slices regressed, including tabs 2, 4, and 6 and higher-popularity item quartiles. Portfolio impact was slightly negative versus the incumbent ensemble and also not significant, so the hypothesis that these temporal-context categorical features would likely add useful portfolio gain is not established by this run.
nodes.why: This is the mandated applicable first-round exploit for the baseline parent and is directly consumable by the current backend. DeepFM benefits from additional categorical context because its interaction mechanism is feature crossing; hour and prior-gap are legal pre-impression pair features that can alter ordering within a user while preserving leakage safety.

nodes.expected: If connected, predictions will differ from the parent on rows with tabs 2/4/6, with possible small standalone change but improved portfolio marginal contribution through rank diversity on those slices.
nodes.hypothesis: A small tab-specific monotone recalibration will improve marginal portfolio contribution by shifting ordering in weak tabs 2/4/6 where the current parent underperforms, while preserving most of the parent's strong global ordering.
nodes.label: tab-aware score calibration at prediction
nodes.lesson: Predict-time tab-only affine calibration is too crude here; prefer a stronger train-time interaction mechanism over further hand-tuned tab score shifts.
nodes.result: The experiment successfully changed predictions versus the parent, so the predict-time tab-aware affine calibration was implemented and active. However, the core hypothesis is not supported by trusted evaluation: standalone delta was only +0.000101 with a 95% paired CI spanning zero, and portfolio delta was slightly negative (-3.37e-05), also with CI spanning zero. Diagnostic slice feedback also failed to show the intended targeted improvement on weak tabs 2/4/6: tab 2 and 4 remained negative and tab 6 was neutral, while gains appeared more on other dimensions such as item-popularity slices. Thus the mechanism produced measurable ranking changes, but evidence does not establish that tab-specific posthoc calibration improved weak-tab contribution or portfolio value.
nodes.why: Within-user metrics are unaffected by per-user constants but can change under candidate-specific transformations. Since tab is an allowed inference-time context field and diagnostics identify tab-specific weaknesses, a bounded tab-aware calibration is a directly connected way to seek error diversity without touching training.

nodes.expected: If the hypothesis is right, official validation primary should rise modestly through better contribution on tabs 0/2/6, with prediction hashes changing for affected rows only.
nodes.hypothesis: A small tab-conditional residual on top of the LambdaRank score will improve marginal portfolio value by nudging the tree member toward slices where current portfolio feedback shows systematic underperformance by tab.
nodes.label: tab-aware prediction residual blend
nodes.lesson: Do not rely on portfolio-relative tab weaknesses alone to set fixed prediction-time tab offsets; require direct standalone slice evidence before adding inference-only residual corrections.
nodes.result: The experiment successfully changed predictions, so the mechanism was implemented and testable, but the evidence does not support a reliable gain. Standalone validation showed only a tiny mean improvement over the search parent (delta_primary 1.54e-05) with a 95% paired CI spanning zero, and paired-vs-incumbent also did not exclude zero. Portfolio impact was slightly negative (-3.37e-05) and not significant. Slice diagnostics show the tab-based residual did not consistently help the intended tabs: tab=2 improved, tab=4 worsened materially, tab=0 worsened slightly, and tab=6 showed no effect. This weakly suggests that hard-coded tab residuals derived from portfolio-relative disadvantages did not transfer cleanly into a useful standalone prediction-time correction.
nodes.why: Because ranking is within-user, a global shift is inert, but a tab-varying residual changes ordering when a user has candidates from multiple tabs. The large tab-specific disadvantages suggest this member's errors are structured by tab rather than random. A prediction-side residual is directly executable, cheap, and targets error diversity without changing the delegated training backend.

nodes.hypothesis: Combine models that make different ranking errors.
nodes.label: Best model combination
nodes.mechanism: exhaustive best-subset within-user rank average over node seed ensembles with bounded 0.1-step global weights with pre-registered label-free tab routing
nodes.why: The combination is kept only when its validation evidence is stronger than the alternatives.

timeline.label: Reproduce the locked validation-only portfolio before LLM search.
